UK food supplier used by Aldi collapses and closes with 662 jobs lost
metadata.contentSnippet: Kanes Foods - which supplied Aldi, Lidl, and Asda with salads, stir-fries, and sauces - has ceased trading after entering administration, with 662 jobs lost.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: UK food supplier used by Aldi collapses and closes with 662 jobs lost
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A major UK food supplier has collapsed into administration and ceased trading, resulting in the loss of more than 650 jobs. Kanes Foods, established in 1989, produced pre-packaged salads, stir-fry products and sauces (with a short shelf life) for major supermarkets, including: After 37 years in business, Kanes Foods has collapsed into administration. Timothy Andrew Higgins, Edward Williams and Helen Wheeler-Jones of PwC were appointed joint administrators on Monday (November 9). Following the appointment, Kanes Foods ceased "with immediate effect", and all 662 employees were made redundant. Joint administrator and director at PwC, Tim Higgins, said: "It is deeply regrettable that a long-established business with a strong reputation has been left with no option but to enter administration, and that so many hard-working employees have lost their jobs as a result. "We recognise how difficult a time this is for employees and their families and we will support those affected through the redundancy process." Kanes Foods had been under financial and operational strain for several years. In June 2025, a failure at its wastewater treatment plant led to approximately £2 million in one-off costs and higher ongoing operating expenses. Further disruption came in August 2026, when drought-related supply issues affected trading during the crucial summer season. The company also faced continued losses, negative cash flow and uncertainty over future demand. Directors explored options such as refinancing and securing new investment, but no viable solutions were found. A fast-track sale process began in mid-September 2026, but administrators were unable to secure a going concern sale in time. Administrators said they will support affected employees in making claims to the Redundancy Payments Service. It has been a tough year for the UK high street, with several retailers entering administration or liquidation and others announcing widespread store closures. Major high street brands Claire's and Quiz have been forced to close all their remaining stores after falling into administration. UK fashion retailer Leading Labels is also set to close its remaining 15 stores after falling into liquidation in May. Whitbread closed all its standalone branded restaurants across the UK last month, affecting five brands: However, Queensway Inns and Common Table Group have now taken over 110 of these former Whitbread sites, saving them from closure. Poundland has filed a notice to appoint administrators, putting the future of its 150 stores and 11,000 employees at risk. TG Jones and the British Heart Foundation will also be closing around 150 stores each across the UK. Wynsors World of Shoes is shutting 17 stores across the UK, with closing down sales already underway at several affected branches. UK entertainment retailer Zavvi has ceased trading after nearly 20 years, having collapsed into administration for a second time. Australian stationery retailer Typo is also set to pull out of the UK in 2027, closing all its stores and ending online trading. Other retailers have been forced to close stores this year, including: Several UK travel companies have ceased trading or entered administration in 2026, including: Wayfairer Travel Limited has also suspended all services "until further notice" as it looks to appoint an administrator. Meanwhile, four UK airlines have fallen into administration or liquidation: Meanwhile, UK delivery company Yodel was phased out completely in July after being acquired by InPost. Iconic fashion brand Nasty Gal has also shut down its website after being sold by Debenhams in a deal worth around £12 million (US$16 million). It hasn't all been bad news for the UK high street, with several major brands announcing new store openings for 2026, including Joules, B&M, Aldi, M&S, and Superdrug. Meanwhile, brands including Evans and Bodycare have returned to the UK high street this year after previously closing all their stores. Which store/business closure in 2026 has impacted you the most? Let us know in the poll above or in the comments below.

metadata.title: Budget supermarket crowned best own-label range again, beating M&S and Waitrose
metadata.contentSnippet: Aldi has beaten M&S, Waitrose and Sainsbury's to a major food award for its Specially Selected range, with 17 medals including three golds.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Budget supermarket crowned best own-label range again, beating M&S and Waitrose
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Aldi has beaten more expensive supermarket rivals including M&S, Waitrose and Sainsbury's after its premium own-brand food range was named the best in the country for the second year running. The discount supermarket's Specially Selected range has been crowned Own Label Range of the Year at the Quality Food Awards (QFAs), with judges recognising its food quality across a wide range of products. Aldi also took home 17 medals in total – including three golds, eight silvers and six bronzes – putting it ahead of some of the UK's biggest grocery names. The results will be particularly welcome news for shoppers looking to buy premium food without paying the prices often associated with higher-end supermarket ranges. The Quality Food Awards are judged by a panel of industry experts, including chefs, food scientists and food writers. Products are assessed on factors including ingredients, taste, aroma, packaging and value for money. Aldi Specially Selected mince pies (Image: Aldi) Among Aldi's biggest winners were three products that secured gold medals in their respective categories. Its Specially Selected Premium Wagyu Denver Steaks, priced at £6.99 for 227g, won Best Beef, while the £3.69 Gastro Mac & Cheese took the Best Ready Meals title. The supermarket also won Best Smoked Fish for its Specially Selected Lightly Smoked Scottish Salmon Fillets, which cost £4.29 for 240g. Recommended reading: All three products are available in Aldi stores now. Other familiar products from the range also received recognition, with silver medals awarded to: Aldi's latest award follows another successful year at the Quality Food Awards. The retailer was named QFA Christmas Retailer of the Year in September, while its Specially Selected East Anglian Fresh Whole Goose, priced at £11.99 per kg, won Christmas Product of the Year. Aldi Specially Selected crisps (Image: Aldi) Julie Ashfield, Chief Commercial Officer at Aldi UK, said: "Our team of buyers and suppliers work hard all year to ensure our Specially Selected range is the best for both quality and price - and being named Own Label Range of the Year by the prestigious QFAs is fantastic recognition of that, and proof that shoppers don’t have to pay more to eat well. "We’re particularly delighted to retain the title for a second year running - it’s a wonderful way to round off a fantastic year."

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Government confirms new State Pension rates – see how much pensioners will get
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Pensioners are set to receive a higher weekly State Pension from April 2027 after the Government announced the new payment rates for the next financial year. The full new State Pension will increase to £250.70 a week, up from £241.30, while the full basic State Pension will rise to £192.10 a week from £184.90. The increases amount to an extra £9.40 and £7.20 a week respectively, giving eligible pensioners hundreds of pounds more over the course of a year. The new figures have been set out in a House of Commons Library briefing published on Wednesday, November 11, covering the benefit and pension rates announced for the 2027/28 financial year. Both the basic and new State Pension will rise by 3.9% from April 2027, in line with the annual increase in average weekly earnings between May and July 2026. The increase is part of the Government's commitment to the State Pension triple lock, which means payments rise each year by the highest of inflation, average earnings growth or 2.5%. The full weekly rates will be: Over a full year, the increase works out at around £488.80 for someone receiving the full new State Pension and £374.40 for someone receiving the full basic State Pension. The new State Pension applies to people who reached State Pension age on or after April 6, 2016. The basic State Pension is the core payment under the old State Pension system, for people who reached State Pension age before that date. The figures are the full weekly rates. The amount an individual receives will depend on their National Insurance record and whether they qualify for the full entitlement. Recommended reading: Pension Credit is also set to rise by 3.9% from April 2027, with the standard minimum guarantee increasing to: Pension Credit is a means-tested benefit designed to top up the income of people who have reached State Pension age and are on a lower income. It can also provide access to other support, including help with housing costs and some health-related expenses.

metadata.title: Millions could be affected by DWP benefits decision – full limits revealed
metadata.contentSnippet: The DWP plans to freeze the Benefit Cap for 2027/28. See the proposed weekly, monthly and annual limits for couples and single households.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Millions could be affected by DWP benefits decision – full limits revealed
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The DWP has revealed they plan to freeze the maximum amount Brits can claim in benefits from next year. The Department for Work and Pensions updated their website on Wednesday, November 11, to outline proposed benefits rates for the 2027-28 tax year. Benefits caps are used by the government to limit the total amount of money claimants can receive and it applies to most people over 16 and below State Pensions age. -Widowed Parent’s Allowance (or Widowed Mother’s Allowance or Widow’s Pension if you started getting it before 9 April 2001) The current annual maximum for couples (with or without children) or single claimants with a child of qualifying age is £22,020 or £25,323 for those in Greater London. The annual maximum for single adults households this tax year, which ends in April, is £14,753 or £16,967 in Greater London. This is proposed to be frozen for the 2027-28 tax year, meaning Brits won't be able to claim more than this amount between April 2027 and 2028. The monthly equivalent is also planned to be frozen at £1,835 and £2,110.25 (Greater London) for couples, with or without children, or single claimants with a child of qualifying age. Single households without children face the same freeze, with the maximum remaining at £1,229.42 and £1,413.92 in Greater London. Weekly equivalents are planned to remain at £423.46 and £486.98 (Greater London) for couples, with or without children, or single claimants with a qualifying-age. The weekly maximum for single households is planned to remain at £283.71 or £326.29 (Greater London). This is despite the Office for National Statistics' most recent inflation rate being recorded at 3.6% in September and many economists forecasting that this is expected to rise next year. The government explains that the cap may not start for nine months if someone is claiming Universal Credit but this depends on their earnings. Recommended reading: Brits are not affected by the benefits cap if they or their partner get Universal Credit because of a disability that 'stops them from working' or get it because they care for someone with a disability. They're also exempt if they get Universal Credit and they or their partner earn £881 or more a month combined, after tax and National Insurance contributions.

metadata.title: 2 Tesco products recalled as shoppers warned 'do not eat' them
metadata.contentSnippet: Two pie products sold at Tesco have been recalled due to incorrect labelling, posing a health risk to some shoppers.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 2 Tesco products recalled as shoppers warned 'do not eat' them
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Two pie products sold at Tesco have been recalled due to the packaging being labelled incorrectly. The affected items are the Tesco Steak and Guinness Pie (200g) and the Tesco 6 Steak and Guinness Mini Pies (198g). These items contain milk but their packaging does not declare it, posing a possible risk to anyone who is allergic to milk or has an intolerance to milk or milk constituents. All use-by dates of both products up to and including November 23, 2026 are being recalled. Friday 13 November - Tesco recalls various Tesco Steak and Guinness Pie products because of undeclared milk https://t.co/rbMS6CajIu #FoodAllergy https://t.co/iRhHJzurDg https://t.co/IUIXhKJIBY — Food Standards Agency (@foodgov) November 13, 2026 The Food Standards Agency (FSA) has warned customers: “If you have bought any of the above products and have an allergy or intolerance to milk or milk constituents, do not eat them.” Instead, customers must return them to the Tesco store where they bought them so they can get a full refund. No receipt is needed to receive the refund and if you need more information, you can use Tesco’s contact page to get in touch. Tesco reassured customers that no other products are affected by this recall and apologised for any inconvenience to customers. The FSA explains what an allergy alert is and why they are issued: “Sometimes there will be a problem with a food product that means it should not be sold. “Then it might be 'withdrawn' (taken off the shelves) or 'recalled' (when customers are asked to return the product). Recommended reading: “Sometimes foods have to be withdrawn or recalled if there is a risk to consumers because the allergy labelling is missing or incorrect or if there is any other food allergy risk. “When there is a food allergy risk, the FSA will issue an Allergy Alert.” Do you shop at Tesco? Let us know in the comments below.

metadata.title: UK airline ordered into compulsory liquidation 7 years after being founded
metadata.contentSnippet: The virtual UK airline Global Airlines has been ordered into compulsory liquidation seven years after it was founded in 2019

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: UK airline ordered into compulsory liquidation 7 years after being founded
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Global Airlines has been ordered into compulsory liquidation following a winding-up petition. The UK startup, which planned to use a fleet of Airbus A380 planes, was formally ordered to wind up by the Insolvency and Companies Court on Wednesday, November 4. The winding-up petition was originally filed in May, with several hearings held in the following months, including the most recent in October. The Gazette published the notice on Thursday, November 12, confirming the order. Former company directors Tom Stokely and Prashant Uttamchandani joined the case as supporting creditors and were represented by the law firm Katten Muchin Rosenman. With the order now in place, an officer of the court—known as the official receiver—has taken control of winding up the company. Government guidelines state that once a winding-up order is issued, the company’s bank accounts are typically frozen and its assets sold off to repay creditors. Companies have the right to apply for cancellation of a winding-up order within five working days if they believe the action is unwarranted. As of the latest update, Global Airlines is still listed as active on Companies House, though its most recent accounts are overdue. Global Airlines has been contacted by Newsquest for comment. Global Airlines Limited operated as a virtual airline with ambitions to operate a fleet of four Airbus A380 aircraft. The company, which was founded in 2019, acquired its only aircraft in May 2023, and claimed to be the first new A380 owner in eight years. Its maiden flight, operated under a damp lease from Hi Fly Malta, flew from Glasgow to New York-JFK on May 15, 2025. After completing just four transatlantic flights, the aircraft was placed into long-term storage in Tarbes, France, on July 16, 2025, with no known return-to-service date. Discussing its vision for the company, Global Airlines shared: "We want to deliver the Best Way to Fly. "And whether flying Global Traveller, Business or First, we believe we will. "Flying to a variety of destinations all over the world, we will breathe new life into onboard product and service, working with some amazing brands, delivering genuine value for money for our passengers. "And by embracing the latest technology and deploying it across every touch point, we can work smarter and deliver a Global experience that is unique to you." Recommended reading: Several UK travel companies have ceased trading or entered administration in 2026, including: Meanwhile, four UK airlines have fallen into administration or liquidation: Wayfairer Travel Limited has also suspended all services "until further notice" as it looks to appoint an administrator. Have you been on a Global Airlines flight before? Let us know in the comments.

metadata.title: DWP disability benefit increase from 2027 for people who need care or mobility help
metadata.contentSnippet: The DWP has confirmed new Universal Credit rates from April 2027, with payments rising for people who need care or help with mobility

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: DWP disability benefit increase from 2027 for people who need care or mobility help
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The DWP revealed that a million Brits could receive more Disability Living Allowance money from April next year. The Department for Work and Pensions updated their website on November 11 with proposals to increase the weekly payments. The current rates only cover the tax year between April 6 2026 and April 5 2027 so from April 6 next year new rates will apply. These increases are labelled as 'provisional' but the Government website's update history shows the previous provisional figures reflected the final figures to the penny. Disability Living Allowance, which helps cover the costs of extra personal care or mobility, has two components - care and mobility. Both of these are split from highest to lowest rates of payment depending on how severe the need for support is. People are eligible for the care component if they need help with things like washing, eating, cooking, communicating needs, dressing or using the toilet. They may also need supervision to 'avoid putting yourself or others in danger' or to have dialysis. The highest rate is paid to those who need 'help or supervision throughout both day and night, or if a medical professional has said they're nearing the end of their life'. This payment is proposed to rise from the £114.60 per week being paid during the current tax year to £118.60 per week for the 2027-28 tax year. The middle rate is described as being suitable for those who need 'frequent help or constant supervision during the day, supervision at night or someone to help you while on dialysis'. The lowest rate is for those who 'need help for some of the day or with preparing cooked meals' and this rate is proposed to increase from £30.30 per week to £31.35. The mobility component is for people who either cannot walk, can only walk 'short distances without severe discomfort' or who could become 'very ill if they try to walk'. People may also get this if they have no feet or legs, are 100% blind or you were between ages 3-64 on April 11 2011 and have been certified as 'severely sight impaired'. Recommended reading: Other criteria include those at least 80% deaf, those who need someone with them when outdoors or those who are 'severely mentally impaired' with behavioural problems. The lower rate of payment is for those who need 'guidance or supervision outdoors' and this would rise from £30.30 per week to £31.35 in the 2027-28 tax year. The higher rate is for those who have 'any other, more severe, walking difficulty' than covered in the lower rate and this would increase from £80 to £82.80 under the proposed new rates. Payments are usually sent directly to claimants bank accounts every four weeks and if their circumstances change they are told to contact the Disability Service Centre.

metadata.title: MoneySavingExpert warns Virgin customers to check for 'sneaky' paid add-on
metadata.contentSnippet: MoneySavingExpert says Virgin Experience Days shoppers should check for a £9.99 annual membership they may not have intended to buy.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: MoneySavingExpert warns Virgin customers to check for 'sneaky' paid add-on
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Virgin Experience Days shoppers are being urged to check whether they were signed up to a paid membership without realising. MoneySavingExpert said its team found the £9.99-a-year Memory Makers+ subscription was being added to orders through a pre-ticked box at checkout. The consumer website said it spotted the issue when it visited the company's website on October 30 and reported it to the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA). MoneySavingExpert said Virgin Experience Days changed its website after the issue was raised, so the membership box was no longer selected by default. The membership offers discounts on purchases, free greeting cards and other benefits, and renews automatically each year. CMA guidance says businesses must obtain a customer's express consent before charging for optional extras. It says a pre-ticked box does not provide that consent when a customer must take action to avoid an extra charge. The regulator also says customers who did not expressly agree to an additional charge are legally entitled to claim a refund. MoneySavingExpert recommends searching email inboxes, including junk and spam folders, for an account activation message to check whether the membership was added. It advises customers who want to cancel or request a refund to contact memorymakers@virginexperiencedays.co.uk. A Virgin Experience Days spokesperson said: "Memory Makers+ remains a relatively new addition to our business, and we continually review and refine the programme based on performance data, customer feedback and regulatory developments." The company said most customers saved more than the cost of membership on their first purchase and that it received positive feedback about the scheme. The spokesperson added: "In the small number of cases where a customer wishes to cancel, we operate a seven day a week support operation where queries are handled within 24 hours."

metadata.title: Is Microsoft still down? Thousands report issues with Outlook and other apps
metadata.contentSnippet: Microsoft users have reported issues with several apps including Outlook, Microsoft 365, and Teams.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Is Microsoft still down? Thousands report issues with Outlook and other apps
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Microsoft users are still reporting issues with several of its services including Outlook. People have taken to Downdetector to report the issues with over 3,000 reports being made at around 6pm last night (Thursday, November 12). The number of reports of Microsoft Outlook being down is currently rising again with 1,115 reports being made at 6am this morning (Friday, November 13). 29% of people have reported issues with logging in to Outlook while 26% have said they are struggling to receive messages and 23% are having issues with the app. We're investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas. More details can be found in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543. — Microsoft 365 Status (@MSFT365Status) November 12, 2026 Microsoft released a statement yesterday sharing that the issues with its apps started in the US but has spread to areas across the world. Microsoft said: “We're investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas. More details can be found in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543. “While we’re working to mitigate impact, we’ve confirmed the issue may affect Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region, more information will be provided in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543. “We’ve determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors. “We're providing more information under EX1550543 and MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center, as well as https://status.cloud.microsoft.” As well as Outlook, Microsoft users are facing issues with several other apps including Microsoft 365 with over 600 people reporting issues this morning. Over 100 people have taken to Downdetector and have reported issues with Teams. Others have reported issues with Copilot and the Microsoft store. Microsoft has confirmed the fixes are not going "as expected" with the team still trying to find new ways to restore its services. It has tried several solutions to the problem such as isolating parts of its infrastructure and shifting traffic to alternate routes. Charles Lamanna, Microsoft's executive vice-president, has said the outages do not appear to be because of a cyber attack. Microsoft said: “We’ve monitored the status of the changes applied to improve serviceability and confirmed that change is not taking as expected." Downdetector is a website that allows users of popular services like Instagram, Facebook, and Virgin Media to share if they are having trouble with the services. Describing itself on its website, Downdetector is “where people go when services don’t work.” The site will also collect information about any service problems from social media and other factors on the web. An incident is detected if the number of reports is significantly higher than the typical average for that service. Have you been struggling to access Microsoft services? Let us know in the comments.

metadata.title: M&S apologises after customer ate 'crispy moth' lurking in tortilla chips
metadata.contentSnippet: Suzanne Bailey says she found a moth in M&S tortilla crisps served with a family meal. M&S apologised and said it was investigating.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: M&S apologises after customer ate 'crispy moth' lurking in tortilla chips
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A woman says she found a moth in her M&S tortilla crisps after eating a third of the bag. Suzanne Bailey said she initially thought the object was a burnt tortilla when she served the crisps with a family meal. The 45-year-old said she then realised it was a moth, which she believed had been cooked with the crisps. M&S apologised, offered her a refund and said it was investigating with its supplier. The operations manager, from Liverpool, had bought a £1.25 bag of lightly salted tortilla crisps for a Mexican meal. She said her 13-year-old daughter Isabella had eaten one crisp and was sick after the discovery. Ms Bailey said: "I went to pick the burnt tortilla up and this is when I realised it was a moth. My little girl had a mouthful of food and threw up. "I was mortified as I had eaten approximately a third of the bag." She said she found what she believed were the moth's legs when she returned the crisps to the bag as evidence, leaving her concerned she might have eaten one. Ms Bailey added: "It's gross and absolutely disgusting. I'm not into bushtucker trials but it feels like I've done an M&S one. "We haven't been back to shop at M&S. I don't think I could eat tortilla chips again either." After the incident, she threw away the £10 meal and ordered a £20 takeaway to feed her family instead. After taking photographs, she said she submitted a complaint through the M&S website and called customer support. An M&S spokesperson said: "We take matters like this extremely seriously and are working closely with our supplier partner to investigate this fully." The spokesperson said: "We have been in touch with the customer directly to apologise for the inconvenience caused and offer a full refund."

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Royal Mint Beatrix Potter 50p coin sells for more than 400 times face value on eBay
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Royal Mint Peter Rabbit 50p coin has sold on eBay for more than £200. The Royal Mint's Beatrix Potter collection began in 2016, marking 150 years since the author's birth. The first Peter Rabbit design showed a close-up of the character facing forward, complete with whiskers. Other 2016 designs featured Squirrel Nutkin, Mrs Tiggy-Winkle and Jemima Puddle-Duck. Four more designs arrived in 2017, featuring Tom Kitten, Benjamin Bunny, Jeremy Fisher and another Peter Rabbit. The 2018 Peter Rabbit and Flopsy Bunny designs each had a circulating mintage of 1.4 million. The Peter Rabbit editions from 2019 and 2020 were not put into general circulation. The seller described the coin as a 2016 Royal Mint Peter Rabbit 50p in silver proof, with a fineness of 0.925. The listing eventually sold for a total of £219.20, including a £9.03 buyer-protection fee. The Royal Mint lists the 2023 Atlantic Salmon 50p as the rarest circulating 50p, with a mintage of 200,000. Next on its list is the 2009 Kew Gardens 50p, with 210,000, followed by the 2011 Olympic football design, with 1,125,500. The date matters: the Royal Mint's table also records two million Atlantic Salmon 50p coins dated 2025. Other low-mintage circulating designs include the 2011 Olympic wrestling, judo and triathlon coins, alongside the 2018 Peter Rabbit and Flopsy Bunny 50ps. Mintage is the number of coins made, and a lower figure can make a design harder for collectors to find. A coin's condition, design, material and demand from collectors can also affect what someone is willing to pay. A genuine error can be of interest to collectors, but a seller's description alone is not independent verification. The Royal Mint advises buyers of second-hand coins to check for original packaging and, for proof editions, a certificate of authenticity. A specialist valuation can help an owner establish a coin's history and likely value.

metadata.title: PM gives flat owners new powers to challenge 'unfair' service charges
metadata.contentSnippet: Millions of leaseholders are set to gain new powers to challenge unfair service charges.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: PM gives flat owners new powers to challenge 'unfair' service charges
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Millions of leaseholders are set to gain new powers to challenge unfair service charges. The government says more than three million leaseholders in England will benefit from the reforms, with the first changes planned for April 1, 2027. The measures are due to be introduced in stages through to November 2028, subject to parliamentary approval. From April 2027, leaseholders will be able to request information about their service charges, including details from previous years. Landlords will need a good reason to refuse to provide the information, according to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government. Service charges are fees paid by leaseholders or tenants to cover the maintenance, repair and management of shared areas of a building. The ministry says the changes will give leaseholders a clearer picture of how their building is managed, maintained, repaired and insured. The first stage also includes stronger protection against having to pay a landlord's legal costs when challenging a charge. Landlords will need court or tribunal approval to pass on legal costs, while leaseholders will gain a right to recover their own legal expenses, the government says. Further measures are planned for November 1, 2027, when leaseholders will receive clearer information about charges, including details of building insurance and administration fees. There will also be stronger protections against excessive or unreasonable fees for arranging and managing insurance. Private landlords will have to use standardised service charge demand forms and provide financial accounts and annual reports from November 2027. Councils and housing associations will have until November 1, 2028 to introduce those forms, accounts and reports for their leaseholders. Kion Ahadi, chief executive of the Leasehold Advisory Service, said: "Service charges are the most common issue leaseholders contact us about. "We welcome these changes as an important step forward in helping people understand what they are paying for and challenge costs they believe are unfair. "Leaseholders need clear information about how their money is being spent and a fair opportunity to raise concerns. "Better access to that information and stronger protection from landlords’ legal bills will give them more confidence to hold their landlord to account."

metadata.title: DWP Universal Credit claimants face new payment rates - check what you could get
metadata.contentSnippet: The DWP has confirmed new Universal Credit rates from April 2027, with monthly payments rising for single claimants, couples and families with children.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: DWP Universal Credit claimants face new payment rates - check what you could get
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Millions of people claiming Universal Credit are set to receive a higher monthly payment next year, after the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) confirmed the new benefit rates. The Government has published its annual review of benefit payments, setting out how much claimants will receive from April 2027. Working-age and disability benefits will rise by 3.5%, with the new rates mainly coming into effect from April 12, 2027. Inflation-linked benefits and tax credits will rise by 3.5% from April 2027, in line with the annual increase in the Consumer Prices Index (CPI) rate of inflation for September 2026. Universal Credit standard allowances will receive an additional uplift as specified in the Universal Credit Act 2025. The basic and new State Pensions will be uprated by 3.9% from April 2027, in line with the annual increase in the Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) index for May–July 2026. Universal Credit is currently paid to more than 8.4 million people across the UK. Due to the increase in line with CPI, and the additional uprating factor, in 2027/28 Universal Credit standard allowances will increase: Universal Credit is a means-tested benefit designed to help with living costs for people on a low income, out of work or unable to work. The number of people claiming it has increased as the DWP continues its managed migration programme, which is moving people from older benefits onto the newer system. Around 2.2 million Universal Credit claimants are in employment, while a significant number of others are not expected to work because of health conditions or caring responsibilities. Recommended reading: Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden confirmed the increases in a statement to Parliament following the Budget. He said: “The new rates will apply in the tax year 2027-28 and will mainly come into effect from April 12 2027. “The other state pension and benefit rates covered by my statutory review will be increased by 3.5%, in line with the increase in the consumer prices index in the year to September 2026. “This includes most working-age benefits and other benefits for people below state pension age; benefits to help with additional needs arising from disability; statutory payments including statutory sick pay and statutory maternity pay; and additional state pension. The pension credit savings credit maximum amount will also increase by 3.5%.”

metadata.title: Met Police opens investigation into David Walliams after sexual offences allegations
metadata.contentSnippet: The Metropolitan Police has launched an investigation into David Walliams after a number of allegations of serious sexual offences

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Met Police opens investigation into David Walliams after sexual offences allegations
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The Metropolitan Police has launched an investigation after the force received “a number of allegations of non-recent serious sexual offences” against David Walliams. It comes after Walliams was named as the celebrity who tried to block the publication of his identity amid allegations of “inappropriate sexual activities” with girls and young women earlier this week. Multiple women have accused the comedian, 55, of sexually inappropriate behaviour and grooming, including when they were teenagers, according to an investigation by the Guardian and ITV News. Walliams denies all allegations against him. David Walliams has denied all allegatons made against him (Image: Aaron Chown/PA) The Met Police received a number of non-recent allegations against the former Britain’s Got Talent judge “in recent days”. In a statement on Friday (November 13), the Met said the complaints made are separate from those previously reported by ITV News and The Guardian. But it added those reports are being reviewed by officers “to establish whether there is any evidence of offences”. A joint investigation by ITV News and The Guardian alleges Walliams preyed on teenage girls and young women for sexual purposes. Multiple women accuse Walliams of “grooming” them as teenagers, while another described her alleged encounter with Walliams as “sexual assault”. Walliams is also accused of inappropriate conduct and sexual harassment at his former publisher HarperCollins, and while working on Britain’s Got Talent. 🚨 BREAKING: David Walliams is now being investigated by the Met Police over alleged "serious sexual offences" https://t.co/udBrHX7noC — Politics UK (@PolitlcsUK) November 13, 2026 Responding to the ITV and Guardian investigation, Walliams denied all allegations against him. He said: "Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with... I realise I did not always take people’s feelings properly into account. That is something I regret. “And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did... “I am not a sexual predator... I have not broken the law... I am devastated that some of the women I met ten to twenty years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me.” The former Britain’s Got Talent judge, known for appearing in comedy shows including Come Fly With Me and Little Britain alongside Matt Lucas, has sold more than 60 million copies of his children’s books globally. They include The Boy In The Dress, Fing, and Gangsta Granny, the latter of which was turned into a one-hour BBC special in 2013, followed by a sequel starring Sheridan Smith in 2022. Walliams’ book publisher HarperCollins dropped him in December 2025, after an investigation into allegations he had “harassed” young women, which Walliams strongly denied. Earlier this month, theme park Alton Towers permanently closed its World of David Walliams attraction, which featured rides inspired by the books. Walliams left Britain’s Got Talent in 2022 after he apologised for making “disrespectful comments” about auditioning contestants during filming breaks in January 2020 at the London Palladium. In 2023, Britain’s Got Talent producer Fremantle apologised and reached an “amicable resolution” with Walliams after the remarks he made while on the show were leaked.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A school in Sawtry has celebrated double recognition for its work helping pupils develop skills both inside and outside the classroom. Sawtry Village Academy has achieved the Gold Learning Outside the Classroom mark and been reaccredited with the Quality in Careers Standard through Career Mark. The Gold award recognises opportunities provided for pupils to learn in real-world settings, with experiences designed to support academic achievement, personal development, wellbeing and future aspirations. Principal Simon Parsons said achieving the two accreditations at the same time reflected the work taking place across the school. He said: “I am incredibly proud of our entire school community for achieving this remarkable dual recognition. “Securing both the LOtC Gold Mark and the Quality in Careers Standard at the same time is a true testament to the dedication of our staff, the vision of our leaders and the enthusiasm of out students.” Mr Parsons also said the academy believes pupils’ education should extend beyond traditional classroom learning. He added: “By blending rich, real-world learning experiences with exceptional future pathways guidance, we are ensuring our young people leave us as confident, well-equipped and ambitious global citizens.”

metadata.title: Watch moment ATM thief found hiding in loft after nationwide crime spree
metadata.contentSnippet: A prolific thief who targeted cash machines across England and Wales, including Cambridgeshire, has been jailed.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Watch moment ATM thief found hiding in loft after nationwide crime spree
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A prolific thief who targeted cash machines across England and Wales, including Cambridgeshire, has been jailed. Bogdan Gasparov, 40, used cash-trapping devices to steal more than £16,000 from at least 180 ATMs between May and October 2026. Police found him hiding in a loft crawl space during a raid on his Hardie Road home in Dagenham. Detective Sergeant Mike Simpson from ERSOU's Proactive Economic Crime Team (PECT) said: "This was not opportunistic offending. "Gasparov carried out a calculated campaign of theft, targeting cash machines across the country and repeatedly returning to steal money that belonged to unsuspecting customers. "What makes this case even more brazen is that Gasparov had previously been convicted for similar offences and deported from the UK, only to return illegally and resume the same criminal behaviour. "He clearly believed he could stay one step ahead of investigators. He couldn't. "Thanks to the determination of our officers and the strength of the evidence gathered, he has now been brought to justice once again." Gasparov targeted ATMs in Bury St Edmunds, Lowestoft and Sudbury in Suffolk, Great Yarmouth in Norfolk, Huntingdon and Peterborough in Cambridgeshire, and Harlow in Essex. He also struck near Nottingham, Oxford, Somerset, Bristol, Derby, Gloucester, Lincoln and the West Midlands, as well as in parts of Scotland and Wales. The scheme involved Gasparov posing as a legitimate customer, fitting homemade cash-trapping devices to ATMs, and leaving the area. When genuine customers attempted to withdraw money, the cash would become trapped in the device. Gasparov would then return later to retrieve the device and the stolen funds. CCTV from several locations repeatedly placed Gasparov at the scenes. A search of his vehicle uncovered clothing worn during the offences, homemade cash-trapping devices and tools to make them. Moldovan national Gasparov used several aliases and had previous convictions for similar crimes. He had re-entered the UK illegally after being deported. Within 24 hours of his arrest, he pleaded guilty at Chelmsford Magistrates’ Court to two counts of theft from an ATM, covering all the offences. He also admitted entering the UK in breach of a deportation order and possessing items for use in fraud. On November 9, Gasparov was jailed for three years and six months at Chelmsford Crown Court. He is expected to face another deportation hearing after his release.

metadata.title: £195,000 boost for Cambridgeshire victims amid early offender releases
metadata.contentSnippet: Extra support has been made available to victims of crime in Cambridgeshire and Peterborough.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: £195,000 boost for Cambridgeshire victims amid early offender releases
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Extra support has been made available to victims of crime in Cambridgeshire and Peterborough. The support is in response to concerns arising from the Early Release Scheme, which is seeing some offenders released from prison before their full sentence is served. Police and Crime Commissioner Darryl Preston has increased the capacity of the Victim and Witness Hub to ensure timely and comprehensive support for those affected. Darryl said: "I understand the anxiety such news could cause especially for victims of domestic violence. "That's why I am keen to raise awareness of the local offer of support available here in our county to ensure victims feel safe, informed and supported." The Victim and Witness Hub offers emotional and practical support, including referrals to home security services and enhanced emotional support programmes. Victim and Witness Care Co-ordinators can also reconnect individuals with specialist services they have previously used. Victims whose offenders are being released early will be notified and directed to support services in their area. For those worried about personal safety, the Bobby Scheme is available to provide home security assessments and install devices such as locks and video doorbells. Additional funding of £195,000 over two years has been allocated to increase support services. A national Offender Release Helpline, set up by Victim Support, is also available on 0808 168 9280. The helpline operates Monday to Friday from 9am to 5pm, excluding bank holidays. The Early Release Scheme, known as the Progression Model, applies to offenders with fixed-term sentences. It allows part of the sentence to be served in the community under supervision. All individuals released under the scheme are subject to licence conditions and a period of intensive supervision. Victims in Cambridgeshire seeking support can contact the Victim and Witness Hub on 0800 781 6818 or by emailing victimandwitnesshub@cambs.police.uk.

metadata.title: Support for pubs only ‘lip service’ after budget says landlady
metadata.contentSnippet: A Cambridge pub landlady has accused the government of only paying “lip service” to supporting hospitality following the latest budget.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Support for pubs only ‘lip service’ after budget says landlady
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Cambridge pub landlady has accused the government of only paying “lip service” to supporting hospitality following the latest budget. Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey delivered the first budget of Andy Burnham’s government last month, with a number of changes for pubs. This includes raising the threshold for Small Business Rates Relief in England from £12k to £18k – meaning businesses with a rateable value below this will pay no business rates. But pub operators will also face higher wage bills with the national living wage for workers aged 21 and over increasing from £12.71 an hour to £13.21. Both changes will come into effect from April 2027 and alcohol duty will also increase in line with inflation from February 1. Hayley Pellegrini, who runs five pubs in the city with her husband Steve including The Portland Arms and The Alex, said she does not feel small businesses are getting the support they need. The 56-year-old said: “We work ridiculous hours and what we pay ourselves we worked out is probably below minimum wage. “But it’s a case of we just have to suck it up and get on with it. “I don’t feel like we are getting the support we need – they aren’t doing anything, they want to be seen as being pub goers and that but they aren’t doing anything. “It’s not just pubs, it’s small businesses in general – we have friends who have small businesses and they are struggling as well.” She said small businesses are discouraged from expanding as they will lose relief and face higher wage bills from increased national insurance contributions and the rise in wages. Ms Pellegrini said it was harder for them as a living-wage employer, but that they’re “fortunate” to be based in Cambridge with a steady stream of business from students and tourists. She said: “Why am I going to employ someone with no experience, when I could be paying someone with ten years of experience the same? I think we are losing the next generation of hospitality managers, in 10 or 15 years we might find we haven’t brought up the next generation of managers.” She said the government was being “narrowminded” by not considering a reduction in VAT – with more than 400,000 signing the VAT’s the Problem petition to cut it from 20 per cent to 10 per cent, in line with other countries in Europe like France, Spain and Italy. Ms Pellegrini said: “We were hoping that Andy Burnham was actually going to be the one who will do something, but now we think – ‘ah, here we go again’. “What worries me is our retirement – we’re so busy trying to keep the business afloat we aren’t actually able to put anything away for our retirement and we’re going to be a burden on the government. “I work long, unsociable, hours often seven days a week to keep this industry going – who am I doing this for? “The slice of the pie being taken off us is just getting bigger and bigger and bigger. “It seems to be targeted at small businesses while companies like Amazon pay a tiny proportion of tax. “Something needs to be redistributed – the rich are getting richer and the rest of us are working our butts off to try and make a living.”

metadata.contentSnippet: A council wants permission to fly three flags outside its main offices.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Huntingdonshire council seeks consent to fly three flags at Pathfinder House
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A council wants permission to fly three flags outside its main offices. Huntingdonshire District Council is seeking permission from its own planning officers to fly the Emergency Services, Remembrance Day and LGBTQ+ Progress Pride flags each year at Pathfinder House in St Mary’s Street, Huntingdon. Caroline Wilson, who submitted the application on behalf of the council, said: "We have been flying all flags annually before realising we needed consent." Reform UK councillors criticised the council for flying the Progress Pride Flag during Pride Month in June. Reform UK members argued the flag was "divisive" and lacked the necessary planning consent. Cllr Ryan Coogan, Reform group leader, said at the time that councils should not fly "divisive political symbols", particularly where the correct permissions have not been obtained, and stressed that public buildings should represent everyone in the district. The council later admitted it lacked permission to fly the flag, but said it only realised this as the flag was being taken down. A spokesperson for the council said: "The Pride Progress flag is a variant of the original Gilbert Baker Pride flag, adopted widely by members of the LGBTQ+ community and related groups. "In planning terms, the Pride flag benefits from 'deemed consent' under the Town and Country Planning (Control of Advertisements) Regulations 2007 (as amended). "However, the Pride Progress flag is not covered by this provision and therefore requires express consent from the local planning authority." The Progress Pride Flag updates the traditional rainbow design to represent more communities within the LGBTQ+ movement. The council said the flag was taken down to make way for the Armed Forces Day Flag, which was flown in honour of Armed Forces Day on June 27. Reform UK councillors said they raised concerns after being contacted by residents about the flag being displayed on a public building. They said this prompted them to challenge its display. Huntingdonshire District Council first raised a Progress Pride flag at Pathfinder House in June 2022, saying it symbolised representation of everyone in the district.

metadata.title: Hinchingbrooke Hospital plans revised as fresh environmental assessment begins
metadata.contentSnippet: Plans to rebuild Hinchingbrooke Hospital have reached a new stage after North West Anglia NHS Foundation Trust submitted a revised Environmental Impact Assessment Scoping Report to Huntingdonshire District Council.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Hinchingbrooke Hospital plans revised as fresh environmental assessment begins
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. A hospital redevelopment is moving forward with a fresh environmental impact assessment underway. Plans to rebuild Hinchingbrooke Hospital have reached a new stage after North West Anglia NHS Foundation Trust submitted a revised Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Scoping Report to Huntingdonshire District Council (HDC). The report sets out key changes and asks the council for a new EIA Scoping Opinion to inform the Environmental Statement for the planned application. The trust previously secured an EIA Scoping Opinion from HDC in October 2025, based on proposals developed in August 2025. An artist's impression of what the new staff accommodation will look like and what the courtyard area will look like once installed by Zed Pods Ltd. (Image: North West Anglia NHS Foundation Trust) Since then, the scheme has undergone further design changes, prompting the need for a revised EIA. The updated plans include a range of modifications to the original development. These include the removal of the lower ground floor from the new hospital building, the addition of an energy centre north of the main building, and the relocation of the ambulance deck to the south-east of the site. Land at Views Common could be used temporarily as a contractor’s compound during construction, which may last up to eight years, subject to a lease agreement with the owner. The northern car park will remain at ground level, with possible solar canopies added. Plans for a multi-storey car park have been scrapped. A separate application is being prepared for car parking on the adjacent Constabulary Land, which has been removed from the main hospital application. The trust plans to submit an outline application covering new hospital buildings, an energy centre, service and administration facilities, parking, cycle storage, landscaping, drainage and improved access from Views Common Road. It will also cover the phased demolition of existing hospital buildings and the removal of some trees protected by Tree Preservation Orders. Approved enabling works include relocating staff accommodation, demolishing former staff blocks and creating a temporary car park. The trust is seeking separate permission for the Constabulary Land car park to maintain parking capacity during construction. A separate application also covers a new main intake substation to provide the hospital with an independent high-voltage electricity supply. The latest EIA Scoping Report confirms that most environmental topics identified in the 2025 assessment remain relevant. However, archaeology has now been scoped in due to the discovery of ridge and furrow earthworks and the high potential for further archaeological remains at Views Common. It also explains how the project will assess air quality, biodiversity, noise and vibration, transport and access, trees, daylight and sunlight, and wind. The trust is working with HDC, statutory consultees and other stakeholders to keep the planning process on track with the project and policy requirements. The site boundary has been redrawn to reflect the latest design, removing areas covered by separate applications and adding land at Views Common. The report says the development is not vulnerable to major accidents or disasters, so those risks will not be assessed further. That conclusion is based on the site’s location, existing safeguards and lack of nearby hazards such as major pipelines. The report also includes an assessment of how climate change could affect the development and how it can withstand those risks. It considers sudden and long-term climate hazards, the vulnerability of key site elements and existing measures to adapt. The assessment will be developed further as the design progresses. The EIA Scoping Report will support the updated hospital planning application and shape its Environmental Statement. HDC is expected to issue a revised Scoping Opinion after consulting statutory bodies and reviewing the report. Hinchingbrooke is one of seven English hospitals being rebuilt through the national New Hospital Programme because of RAAC, with the new facility expected to open by the end of 2032.

metadata.title: Poundland issues major update as UK stores at risk of closure
metadata.contentSnippet: Poundland has issued an update today (November 12) as it continues to try to secure a potential rescue deal.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Poundland issues major update as UK stores at risk of closure
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Poundland has issued an update today (November 12), following the end of a 10-day period that allowed it to continue to try and secure a potential rescue deal. In recent months, the future of Poundland has been uncertain, with last-ditch efforts hoping to save the struggling retailer. The chain filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators at the end of October, which expired at midnight last night. Asked if the company was going into administration on Thursday, managing director Barry Williams told reporters: “We’re going to go and have a board meeting now to have those conversations.” Now, Poundland has issued an update, informing customers of its future plans. Poundland customers have been assured that its stores are open as normal for at least the next 10 working days. The Board of Poundland Limited said: “Over the past two weeks, Poundland has been operating under the statutory protection of a Notice of Intention (NOI) to appoint Administrators. “Amid an ongoing sale process, and with funding agreed to enable the business to continue trading during this period, the Board of Poundland has today resolved to make an application for a second NOI with a view to identifying the best available prospects for shareholders, creditors and our people. “This extends the current protections over the business for a further 10 working days. “Our stores remain open as usual during this period, and we thank our colleagues, suppliers and customers for their incredible and continued support.” Poundland has roughly 600 shops and 11,000 employees across the UK. Ahead of the announcement, Reform UK deputy leader Richard Tice said: “Hopefully the directors will be able to extend the notice of administration period from tonight to allow time for a deal to be done with a new buyer for Poundland. “This will protect many thousands of jobs and keep an important value retailer on the High Street, for hard-pressed consumers worried about rising bills.” After a meeting with MPs on the Commons Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee, Mr Williams thanked the chain’s staff, whose jobs are at risk. He told Sky News he was “representing 11,000 colleagues” as well as thousands in the broader supply chain and “maybe even the retail industry” at the meeting. Asked whether he could guarantee the security of jobs and keep the business going in the run-up to Christmas, he said there were “no guarantees at this point”. It is understood that Poundland’s owners, Gordon Brothers, have enabled the release of around £10 million of funding for things such as paying staff, taxes and suppliers of stock. The extension to Wednesday’s deadline could mean the prospect of a deal that would satisfy the company’s creditors remains on the table. Advisers have been in talks with parties interested in buying the brand or parts of the business such as swathes of shops. Recommended reading: It has held talks with potential bidders including Tesco over proposals to buy up to 150 stores, and other chains such as Iceland and Lidl. Investment firm Xyra Holdings emerged as a potential buyer for the whole business, while Irish firm Martin Property Group is believed to remain interested. Gordon Brothers previously rejected a takeover offer from Martin Property Group but management named the firm as the preferred bidder last month. Would you like to see Poundland remain on UK high streets? Let us know in the comments below.

metadata.title: HMRC Child Benefit rates to rise in April 2027 - new payment amounts explained
metadata.contentSnippet: HMRC has updated its Child Benefit rates for 2027/28, with millions of parents set to receive higher weekly payments.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: HMRC Child Benefit rates to rise in April 2027 - new payment amounts explained
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: HMRC has revealed that millions of families could receive more money in Child Benefit from next April, with new weekly payment rates now appearing on the Government's website. Parents currently receive £27.05 a week for their eldest or only child, with an additional £17.90 paid for each other child. However, these payments are set to increase again for the 2027/28 tax year, according to an update to the Government's Child Benefit information page on November 10. The provisional figures show that the weekly rate for an eldest or only child will rise to £28, while payments for each additional child are expected to increase to £18.55. This would give families an extra £49.40 a year for their eldest or only child, and an additional £33.80 annually for every other child they claim for. The figures are currently marked as 'provisional', meaning they are not yet confirmed as final rates. However, the Government website's update history shows that previous provisional Child Benefit rates have subsequently matched the final amounts announced. The weekly rate of Guardian's Allowance is also expected to increase, rising from £22.95 in 2026/27 to £23.75 in 2027/28. Guardian's Allowance is an additional payment for people bringing up a child whose parents have died. In some circumstances, it can also be claimed where one parent has died and the surviving parent cannot look after the child. Child Benefit is available to parents or guardians responsible for a child under 16, or under 20 if they remain in approved education or training. Only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child, but there is now no limit on the number of children families can receive payments for. This follows the abolition of the two-child limit in April this year. Previously, the restriction meant parents could generally only claim Child Benefit for a maximum of two children. However, some families may face a tax charge if their earnings exceed the High Income Child Benefit Charge threshold. The charge applies if either parent has an individual income of more than £60,000 in tax years from 2024/25 onwards. For tax years up to and including 2023/24, the threshold was £50,000. Child Benefit is usually paid directly into a claimant's bank account every four weeks. Claiming also provides valuable National Insurance credits, which can help protect a parent's entitlement to the State Pension.

metadata.title: More than one million yellow box fines issued - what are the rules and how to appeal
metadata.contentSnippet: More than a million yellow box junction penalties issued by councils in England and Wales since 2023, the junction rules and how to challenge a notice.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: More than one million yellow box fines issued - what are the rules and how to appeal
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: More than a million yellow box junction penalties have been issued by councils in England and Wales since 2023, research suggests. Used car retailer cinch said 37 councils reported issuing 1,047,472 penalty charge notices between 2023 and 2026, with nearly £58 million in penalty payments also reported. The company sent Freedom of Information requests to 217 authorities across the UK, but the penalty figures reported are not a total for every council or for the whole country. The underlying council responses were not supplied with the release and could not be independently checked. Its figures include 347,614 notices in 2025 and a further 231,458 in 2026 up to July. In Hackney, the number rose from 314 in 2024 to 8,567 in 2025, while Buckinghamshire recorded an increase from 3,618 to 16,120. Liverpool recorded 7,622 notices in 2025, compared with 3,376 the year before, according to the research. At Dennis Road Roundabout in Surrey, the number rose from 1,557 in 2024 to 9,101 in 2025. Cinch said councils had received more than 100,000 challenges since 2023 and accepted over 18,000. Those included 6,954 accepted challenges in Redbridge out of 27,615 received, and 3,582 out of 8,328 in Cardiff. Ben Welham, a motoring expert at cinch, said: "Yellow box junctions help to keep traffic moving, but they can be difficult to navigate, particularly in busy towns and cities where traffic is constantly stopping and starting." Yellow box junctions have criss-cross markings designed to keep traffic from blocking the road. Under rule 174 of the Highway Code, drivers must not enter until their exit road or lane is clear. There is an exception for drivers turning right who are held up only by oncoming traffic or other vehicles waiting to turn right. At a signalled roundabout, drivers must not enter a box unless they can cross it completely without stopping. The Northern Ireland Highway Code sets out the same box-junction rules. Penalty amounts and payment periods depend on the issuing authority, so motorists should check the details on their notice. For example, Newcastle City Council says its yellow box penalty is £70, reduced to £35 if paid within 21 days. In England and Wales, a motorist who believes a council PCN is wrong can make a formal challenge, known as a representation, to the authority that issued it. Cinch says drivers generally have 28 days to challenge a notice and should provide supporting evidence, such as photographs or available camera footage. Check the notice for the applicable deadline and instructions, including how to view any footage. If the authority rejects the formal challenge, GOV.UK says there are 28 days after receiving the rejection notice to appeal to an independent tribunal. The appeal is made to London Tribunals for a PCN issued in London, or the Traffic Penalty Tribunal for one issued elsewhere in England or Wales. Scotland and Northern Ireland have different appeal arrangements, so drivers there should follow the instructions from the issuing body. If an appeal is successful, the PCN is cancelled and the motorist does not have to pay.

metadata.title: Decision looms on 600-home plan for St Neots amid flood of objections
metadata.contentSnippet: A decision looms on a plan for up to 600 new homes on land near Priory Hill Road in St Neots, despite a flood of objections from residents.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Decision looms on 600-home plan for St Neots amid flood of objections
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. A decision looms on a plan for up to 600 new homes in St Neots, despite a flood of objections from residents. The outline application by Bloor Homes for land at Priory Hill, north of St Neots, is set to be considered by Huntingdonshire District Council's (HDC) development management committee on November 16. The 87-hectare site would create a new neighbourhood between Priory Hill Road, Huntingdon Road, the River Great Ouse, and the East Coast Main Line. An illustrative sketch of the land in St Neots where 600 new homes could be built (Image: Bloor Homes) The scheme seeks permission for up to 600 homes, with 40 per cent designated as affordable housing. Alongside the housing, the plans include a community hub, mobility hub, public open space, allotments, walking and cycling routes, landscaping, and associated infrastructure. Around 64 hectares of the site would be retained as green space, including meadows, parkland, wildlife areas, and sustainable drainage features. Developers say the plans would extend Priory Park northwards, creating a new 'Priory Piece', new pedestrian and cycle links, and providing opportunities for a future footbridge across the River Great Ouse connecting to Paxton Pits Nature Reserve and the Ouse Valley Way. The site sits close to Priory Park (Image: Newsquest) For access to the site, the plans would see two new T-junctions introduced on Priory Hill Road. Road speeds would be reduced to 30mph along Priory Hill Road and Huntingdon Road, with additional traffic-calming measures. In addition, the double-mini roundabout at the B1043 Huntingdon Road, Priory Hill Road and Mill Lane intersection would be changed to a staggered T-junction, as the developers claim it had previously been identified as "a safety concern". The double-mini roundabout at Priory Hill Road (Image: Newsquest) The double-mini roundabout near the site could be changed to a staggered T-junction (Image: Newsquest) Members of the development management committee are expected to make a decision on the application at a meeting at 7pm on November 16. Planning officers are recommending that the scheme be approved subject to conditions, or refused if an S106 agreement has not been reached. St Neots Town Council and Little Paxton Parish Council have both lodged objections to the scheme. The town council said it is concerned that "the development would place additional pressure on local services and infrastructure, particularly secondary school provision" and raised additional concerns over loss of agricultural land, flood risk and drainage. Additionally, HDC has received a total of 92 objections from residents. One neighbour wrote: "It would cause demonstrable harm to infrastructure, landscape, biodiversity, and the wellbeing of existing residents. "I therefore respectfully urge Huntingdonshire District Council to refuse planning permission for this development." What do you think about the plans? Leave a comment on this story or contact emily.stevens@newsquest.co.uk

metadata.title: Just under half of children in Huntingdon miss out on NHS dentist visits
metadata.contentSnippet: Practice Radar figures show 53 per cent of children in Huntingdon saw an NHS dentist in the year to March 2026.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Just under half of children in Huntingdon miss out on NHS dentist visits
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Just under half of young children in Huntingdon are missing out on NHS dental care, which is below the national average. Practice Radar figures show 53 per cent of children in Huntingdon saw an NHS dentist in the year to March 2026. That compares with 58 per cent across England when measured on the same basis. The gap is even wider among younger children, with just 41.3 per cent of those aged between one and five in Huntingdon seeing an NHS dentist during the year. The figures come amid ongoing national concerns about access to NHS dentistry, especially for younger children. Practice Radar analysed NHS Business Services Authority data to estimate child dental attendance in all 543 English constituencies. The analysis found large regional differences, with the proportion of children seen by an NHS dentist ranging from 32.2 per cent in the City of London and Westminster to 74.5 per cent in Sheffield Hallam. In 62 constituencies, fewer than half of children saw an NHS dentist during the year. Huntingdon’s 53 per cent rate is five points below the England average, but the area is not among the worst performers. The study also examined tooth decay among five-year-olds, but those figures are reported by council area rather than constituency. In Huntingdonshire, 11.4 per cent of five-year-olds had experienced tooth decay in the 2023/24 survey, compared with 22.4 per cent nationally. Huntingdon is therefore not among the 60 constituencies with below-average NHS dental attendance and significantly higher childhood tooth decay. Practice Radar warned that the two figures cover different geographic areas. The 53 per cent attendance rate covers children living in Huntingdon, while the 11.4 per cent decay rate covers the wider Huntingdonshire council area. The research also examined NHS dental contracts in the area. The analysis included seven NHS general dental contracts in Huntingdon, with a median payment of £34.51 per unit of dental activity (UDA). A UDA is the NHS measure for dental work, with different treatments given different values. Across England, the median constituency had an NHS dentist visit rate of 58.6 per cent for children and 47.5 per cent for one- to five-year-olds. Fewer than 40 per cent of one- to five-year-olds saw an NHS dentist in 111 constituencies. There are signs of improvement across England, with 508 out of 543 constituencies recording a higher proportion of children seen by an NHS dentist compared to two years earlier. However, the researchers emphasised that the figures only cover NHS dental care. Children treated entirely privately are excluded, so the figures do not show how many receive dental care overall. Children are counted by where they live, not where their dentist is based, so some Huntingdon residents may receive care outside the constituency. The analysis used NHS Dental Statistics for England 2025/26, tooth-decay data from the Office for Health Improvement and Disparities and population estimates from the Office for National Statistics. A recent Cambridgeshire MP survey found nearly half of respondents were not registered with an NHS dentist, while about half had paid privately after struggling to access NHS treatment. Local NHS dentists have told an MP that contracts are financially and operationally "unviable", with practices losing money on NHS work and subsidising it through private income.
